title: Create API Gateway Stack and VPC Link with AWS CDK
content:
In this section, we explore the secure architectural pattern connecting Amazon API Gateway into a private corporate network via VPC Link, and write the TypeScript source code for ApiGatewayStack using AWS CDK.
1. Role of API Gateway and VPC Link in Enterprise Architecture In modern, production-grade microservices architectures on AWS:
Zero Trust & Private Isolation: Backend services such as ECS Fargate, DynamoDB, and internal load balancers (ALB/NLB) reside strictly in Private Subnets with no assigned public IP addresses. Eliminating public IPs protects your internal application tiers from direct internet scanning, DDoS, and perimeter attacks. What is a VPC Link? VPC Link is a specialized feature of Amazon API Gateway. When initialized, VPC Link provisions Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) inside the designated private subnets of your VPC. Through these ENIs, API Gateway creates a secure private tunnel to route external requests directly to internal resources, specifically the Network Load Balancer (NLB). Why HTTP API (v2) over REST API (v1)? Lower Latency & Higher Throughput: HTTP API is purpose-built as a lightweight proxy with minimal overhead. Up to 70% Cost Reduction: Highly economical for routing API traffic directly to backend container workloads. First-class native integration (HttpNlbIntegration) with Network Load Balancers in just a few lines of CDK code. 2. Write the API Gateway Stack Definition (api-gate-way-stack.ts) Navigate to IaC-ECS-CDK/cdk/lib and open api-gate-way-stack.ts (or create it). We will construct the stack step-by-step as outlined below:
2.1. Import Modules and Define Interface Props Import the required AWS CDK constructs and define the ApiGatewayStackProps interface to receive dependencies (vpc from VpcStack and nlbListener from NlbStack):
import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { Construct } from 'constructs'; import * as ec2 from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-ec2'; import * as elbv2 from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-elasticloadbalancingv2'; import * as apigwv2 from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-apigatewayv2'; import * as integrations from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-apigatewayv2-integrations'; interface ApiGatewayStackProps extends cdk.StackProps { vpc: ec2.IVpc; nlbListener: elbv2.INetworkListener; // Receives port 80 listener from NlbStack } export class ApiGatewayStack extends cdk.Stack { constructor(scope: Construct, id: string, props: ApiGatewayStackProps) { super(scope, id, props); 2.2. Initialize Security Group and Amazon VPC Link into Private Subnets Provision a dedicated Security Group permitting outbound traffic to the NLB, then establish a secure private tunnel (VPC Link) from API Gateway into the VPC’s private subnets without assigning public IPs to backend services:
// 1. Create a dedicated Security Group for VPC Link (permitting outbound traffic to NLB) const vpcLinkSecurityGroup = new ec2.SecurityGroup(this, 'VpcLinkSecurityGroup', { vpc: props.vpc, description: 'Security group for API Gateway VPC Link to Internal NLB', allowAllOutbound: true, }); // 2. Create VPC Link connecting API Gateway into private VPC subnets with the explicit Security Group const vpcLink = new apigwv2.VpcLink(this, 'HttpVpcLink', { vpc: props.vpc, securityGroups: [vpcLinkSecurityGroup], subnets: { subnetType: ec2.SubnetType.PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS, }, }); Important Note on VPC Link Security Group:
If the securityGroups property is omitted, AWS automatically assigns the VPC’s Default Security Group to the VPC Link Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs). AWS CDK enforces security hardening by disabling all outbound rules on the default security group (restrictDefaultSecurityGroup), causing all VPC Link $\rightarrow$ NLB requests to be dropped and triggering a 503 Service Unavailable (due to 30s timeout). Defining an explicit Security Group completely prevents this failure mode.
2.3. Initialize HTTP API Gateway (v2) and Configure CORS Provision the public HTTP API entry point and configure CORS Preflight for standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE):
// 3. Initialize HTTP API Gateway (v2) with CORS preflight support const httpApi = new apigwv2.HttpApi(this, 'ProductsHttpApi', { apiName: 'fcaj-products-api-enterprise', corsPreflight: { allowHeaders: ['*'], allowMethods: [ apigwv2.CorsHttpMethod.GET, apigwv2.CorsHttpMethod.POST, apigwv2.CorsHttpMethod.PUT, apigwv2.CorsHttpMethod.DELETE, ], allowOrigins: ['*'], }, }); 2.4. Integrate HTTP API with Network Load Balancer (HttpNlbIntegration) Use the native HttpNlbIntegration construct to connect the HTTP API with the NLB port 80 listener through the provisioned VPC Link:
// 4. Connect HTTP API to the NLB Listener through the VPC Link const nlbIntegration = new integrations.HttpNlbIntegration( 'NlbIntegration', props.nlbListener, { vpcLink: vpcLink, method: apigwv2.HttpMethod.ANY, } ); 2.5. Define Catch-All Proxy Route, Root Route, and Export Output Configure a catch-all proxy route /{proxy+} to route all sub-paths and a root route / for base URL requests to the NLB, and emit the public invoke URL to CloudFormation outputs:
// 5. Catch-all proxy route forwarding all sub-paths and methods to NLB httpApi.addRoutes({ path: '/{proxy+}', methods: [apigwv2.HttpMethod.ANY], integration: nlbIntegration, }); // 6. Catch-all route for base URL "/" to prevent 503 errors when calling base Invoke URL httpApi.addRoutes({ path: '/', methods: [apigwv2.HttpMethod.ANY], integration: nlbIntegration, }); // 7. Output the public API Gateway invoke endpoint new cdk.CfnOutput(this, 'ApiEndpoint', { value: httpApi.apiEndpoint, description: 'API Gateway Endpoint', }); } } 2.6. Complete Source Code of api-gate-way-stack.ts Below is the complete implementation of api-gate-way-stack.ts for cross-referencing and deployment:
import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { Construct } from 'constructs'; import * as ec2 from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-ec2'; import * as elbv2 from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-elasticloadbalancingv2'; import * as apigwv2 from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-apigatewayv2'; import * as integrations from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-apigatewayv2-integrations'; interface ApiGatewayStackProps extends cdk.StackProps { vpc: ec2.IVpc; nlbListener: elbv2.INetworkListener; // Receives port 80 listener from NlbStack } export class ApiGatewayStack extends cdk.Stack { constructor(scope: Construct, id: string, props: ApiGatewayStackProps) { super(scope, id, props); // 1. Create a dedicated Security Group for VPC Link (permitting outbound traffic to NLB) const vpcLinkSecurityGroup = new ec2.SecurityGroup(this, 'VpcLinkSecurityGroup', { vpc: props.vpc, description: 'Security group for API Gateway VPC Link to Internal NLB', allowAllOutbound: true, }); // 2. Create VPC Link connecting API Gateway into private VPC subnets with the explicit Security Group const vpcLink = new apigwv2.VpcLink(this, 'HttpVpcLink', { vpc: props.vpc, securityGroups: [vpcLinkSecurityGroup], subnets: { subnetType: ec2.SubnetType.PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS, }, }); // 3. Initialize HTTP API Gateway (v2) with CORS preflight support const httpApi = new apigwv2.HttpApi(this, 'ProductsHttpApi', { apiName: 'fcaj-products-api-enterprise', corsPreflight: { allowHeaders: ['*'], allowMethods: [ apigwv2.CorsHttpMethod.GET, apigwv2.CorsHttpMethod.POST, apigwv2.CorsHttpMethod.PUT, apigwv2.CorsHttpMethod.DELETE, ], allowOrigins: ['*'], }, }); // 4. Connect HTTP API to the NLB Listener through the VPC Link const nlbIntegration = new integrations.HttpNlbIntegration( 'NlbIntegration', props.nlbListener, { vpcLink: vpcLink, method: apigwv2.HttpMethod.ANY, } ); // 5. Catch-all proxy route forwarding all sub-paths and methods to NLB httpApi.addRoutes({ path: '/{proxy+}', methods: [apigwv2.HttpMethod.ANY], integration: nlbIntegration, }); // 6. Catch-all route for base URL "/" to prevent 503 errors when calling base Invoke URL httpApi.addRoutes({ path: '/', methods: [apigwv2.HttpMethod.ANY], integration: nlbIntegration, }); // 7. Output the public API Gateway invoke endpoint new cdk.CfnOutput(this, 'ApiEndpoint', { value: httpApi.apiEndpoint, description: 'API Gateway Endpoint', }); } } 3. Detailed Property Breakdown new ec2.SecurityGroup(this, 'VpcLinkSecurityGroup', ...):
Provisions a dedicated Security Group for the VPC Link network interfaces with allowAllOutbound: true. Guarantees that VPC Link can dispatch TCP traffic to the private IP address of the Network Load Balancer on port 80 without interference from default SG restrictions. new apigwv2.VpcLink(..., { securityGroups: [vpcLinkSecurityGroup] }):
Provisions VPC Link network interfaces inside private subnets (ec2.SubnetType.PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS) bound to our explicit Security Group. AWS manages the private tunnel bridging the public API Gateway service and your internal VPC environment securely. new apigwv2.HttpApi(...):
Creates an HTTP API v2 named fcaj-products-api-enterprise. Configures corsPreflight: Permits standard headers (allowHeaders: ['*']) and REST methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) so single-page applications (React, Vue, Angular) can communicate with your backend without CORS restrictions. new integrations.HttpNlbIntegration(...):
Native construct in AWS CDK v2 for HTTP APIs. Binds nlbListener (forwarded from NlbStack) with the vpcLink. Incoming API Gateway requests are packaged and proxied directly to the NLB port 80 over the private link. httpApi.addRoutes({ path: '/{proxy+}' }) & httpApi.addRoutes({ path: '/' }):
/{proxy+}: Catches all sub-resource requests (/actuator/health, /api/products, /api/products/{id}, etc.) and forwards them to Spring Boot. /: Catches root base URL requests, eliminating unexpected 503 errors when users test the base invoke URL directly. cdk.CfnOutput:
Prints the ApiEndpoint URL (https://<api-id>.execute-api.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com) to CloudFormation outputs and the terminal for immediate testing with Postman or curl. Architectural Flexibility: Thanks to the Catch-all proxy (/{proxy+}), adding new Spring Boot controllers (e.g. /api/orders, /api/users) requires zero modifications to API Gateway or CDK code. All routing logic is seamlessly handled downstream by Spring Boot and the Application Load Balancer!

title: Create DynamoDB Stack with AWS CDK
content:
In this section, we will learn how to build a NoSQL database with Amazon DynamoDB using AWS CDK (TypeScript) to store product catalog data for the Spring Boot microservice.
1. Role of DynamoDB in the Microservice Architecture Within our backend application architecture:
Spring Boot Microservice: Provides CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) REST APIs for the product catalog via the /api/products endpoint.
Amazon DynamoDB: Serves as a high-performance serverless NoSQL database. DynamoDB completely eliminates the operational burden of server management, requires no cluster provisioning, and automatically replicates data across 3 Availability Zones within the Region for high availability.
Connection with ECS Fargate: The ECS Fargate cluster requires permissions to access the DynamoDB table. Therefore, separating the DynamoDB table into an independent CDK Stack (DynamoDbStack) allows us to share the table object with EcsStack, thereby granting read/write IAM permissions (grantReadWriteData) to the Task Role explicitly and securely.
2. Write DynamoDB Stack Source Code (dynamodb-stack.ts) Navigate to the directory IaC-ECS-CDK/cdk/lib and open the file dynamodb-stack.ts (or create it if not present). Update the contents defining the DynamoDB stack:
import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { Construct } from 'constructs'; import * as dynamodb from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-dynamodb'; export class DynamoDbStack extends cdk.Stack { public readonly table: dynamodb.Table; constructor(scope: Construct, id: string, props?: cdk.StackProps) { super(scope, id, props); this.table = new dynamodb.Table(this, 'ProductsTable', { tableName: 'products', partitionKey: { name: 'id', type: dynamodb.AttributeType.STRING, }, billingMode: dynamodb.BillingMode.PAY_PER_REQUEST, // On-Demand: Pay per request, zero idle maintenance fees removalPolicy: cdk.RemovalPolicy.DESTROY, // Clean up table on stack deletion during lab cleanup }); new cdk.CfnOutput(this, 'TableName', { value: this.table.tableName, description: 'DynamoDB Table Name', exportName: 'ProductsTableName', }); } } 3. Detailed Explanation of Core Properties public readonly table: dynamodb.Table;:
Declares a public property so that the DynamoDB table instance can be passed to other stacks via props in the bin/cdk.ts file. This allows EcsStack to execute the command props.table.grantReadWriteData(fargateService.taskDefinition.taskRole) without hardcoding ARNs or manually configuring IAM policies. tableName: ‘products’:
Identifier name of the table on DynamoDB. This name matches the table name configured in the repository layer of the Spring Boot application. partitionKey: { name: ‘id’, type: dynamodb.AttributeType.STRING }:
Configures the unique Partition Key (Hash Key) for the table as the id field with string data type (STRING / UUID). DynamoDB uses this id value to distribute data evenly across physical partitions, ensuring constant-time $O(1)$ query speed. billingMode: dynamodb.BillingMode.PAY_PER_REQUEST:
On-Demand Capacity Mode. Unlike the traditional mode (Provisioned) which requires pre-configuring Read Capacity Units (RCU) and Write Capacity Units (WCU), On-Demand automatically scales to accommodate traffic bursts instantly and incurs no charges when there are no reads/writes. This is the ideal choice for learning environments, experimentation, and microservices with fluctuating traffic. removalPolicy: cdk.RemovalPolicy.DESTROY:
By default in AWS CDK, DynamoDB tables are protected by the RETAIN policy (keeping data even if the stack is deleted). In a practice/lab environment, we set it to DESTROY so that when running the cleanup command (cdk destroy), the DynamoDB table is completely deleted automatically, avoiding leftover resources incurring unexpected costs. cdk.CfnOutput:
Outputs the table name to CloudFormation Outputs and the terminal screen for easy verification and integration. Architectural Tip: Separating the database into an independent DynamoDbStack from EcsStack adheres to the principle of Separation of Concerns. You can redeploy, update, or scale the Fargate container application without affecting the lifecycle and persisted data stored in DynamoDB.

title: Create VPC and NAT Gateway with AWS CDK
content:
In this step, we will learn about the network architecture required for containerized applications running on Amazon ECS Fargate and write the stack source code to create a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), Subnets, and NAT Gateway using AWS CDK (TypeScript).
1. Network Architecture for ECS Fargate The network infrastructure of the system is designed according to a standard multi-layer security model:
VPC spanning 2 Availability Zones (AZs): Ensures High Availability. If one Data Center experiences an incident, the system continues to operate on the remaining AZ. Public Subnets: Connected directly to the Internet Gateway. In this lab, Public Subnets are used to host the NAT Gateway. Private Subnets (with Egress): An isolated network area used to place ECS Fargate Tasks and the Internal Load Balancer. Containers in Private Subnets cannot be accessed directly from the public Internet (enhancing security). Containers can still reach the Internet via the NAT Gateway to pull Docker images from Amazon ECR, send metrics/logs to Amazon CloudWatch, and access other AWS services. NAT Gateway (natGateways: 1): Provides one-way outbound Internet access for containers in Private Subnets. In the lab environment, only 1 NAT Gateway is configured and shared across both AZs to minimize costs. In a Production environment, it is recommended to place 1 NAT Gateway per AZ to ensure independent redundancy, or configure VPC Endpoints for internal AWS services. 2. Write VPC Stack Source Code (vpc-stack.ts) Navigate to the directory IaC-ECS-CDK/cdk/lib and open the file vpc-stack.ts (or create it if not present). Update the contents defining the VPC stack:
import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { Construct } from 'constructs'; import * as ec2 from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-ec2'; export class VpcStack extends cdk.Stack { public readonly vpc: ec2.Vpc; constructor(scope: Construct, id: string, props?: cdk.StackProps) { super(scope, id, props); this.vpc = new ec2.Vpc(this, 'VpcLab', { vpcName: 'ecs-cdk-vpc', maxAzs: 2, // A single NAT Gateway is a balanced choice for labs: ECS runs in private subnets // but still pulls images from ECR and sends logs to CloudWatch. // Production should consider NAT per AZ or VPC endpoints. natGateways: 1, subnetConfiguration: [ { cidrMask: 24, name: 'PublicSubnet', subnetType: ec2.SubnetType.PUBLIC, }, { cidrMask: 24, name: 'PrivateSubnet', subnetType: ec2.SubnetType.PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS, }, ], }); new cdk.CfnOutput(this, 'VpcId', { value: this.vpc.vpcId, description: 'VPC ID', }); } } 3. Detailed Explanation of Properties public readonly vpc: ec2.Vpc;: Declares the public vpc variable so this network object can be passed to subsequent Stacks (such as EcsStack, NlbStack, ApiGatewayStack) to share the same network infrastructure.
vpcName: ’ecs-cdk-vpc’: Sets a clear, explicit name for the VPC on the AWS Management Console.
maxAzs: 2: AWS CDK will automatically select 2 available Availability Zones in the current Region (for example: ap-southeast-1a and ap-southeast-1b).
natGateways: 1: CDK will automatically create 1 NAT Gateway, 1 Elastic IP (EIP) placed in the first Public Subnet, and configure the route 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to the NAT Gateway for all Private Subnets.
subnetConfiguration:
PublicSubnet (ec2.SubnetType.PUBLIC): CIDR mask /24 (providing 256 IP addresses per subnet), automatically attached to the Internet Gateway. PrivateSubnet (ec2.SubnetType.PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS): CIDR mask /24, outbound Internet traffic routed through the NAT Gateway. cdk.CfnOutput: Prints the identifier VpcId (vpc-xxxxxx) to the terminal screen upon successful deployment.

title: Deploying Spring Boot on ECS Fargate with AWS CDK TypeScript
content:
Deploying Spring Boot on ECS Fargate with AWS CDK TypeScript This lab guides you on how to package a Spring Boot application into a Docker image, store the image in Amazon ECR, and use AWS CDK written in TypeScript to provision infrastructure running the application on Amazon ECS Fargate.
Throughout the lab, CloudFormation executes the templates generated by CDK. The application runs inside Fargate tasks in private subnets, accessed via an internal Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, and API Gateway HTTP API through a VPC Link.
The core flow of the system is: the Spring Boot application is packaged into an image, the image is pushed to ECR, CDK provisions VPC/ECS/DynamoDB/API Gateway, ECS pulls the image and runs tasks, then requests flow from API Gateway through VPC Link, NLB, and ALB to Spring Boot.
This lab is written based on the current IaC-ECS-CDK repository, using Maven for Spring Boot and TypeScript for CDK. Please follow the order of the items in the navigation bar and always verify local steps before deploying to AWS.

title: Initialize CDK and Write ECR Stack
content:
In this step, we will initialize an AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK) project using TypeScript from the parent directory IaC-ECS-CDK, install the necessary construct libraries, and write the stack source code to create an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) repository.
1. Overall Project Structure Recall the directory structure of the IaC-ECS-CDK project:
IaC-ECS-CDK/ ├── fcaj-spring/ # Spring Boot application source code and Dockerfile (created in steps 2.3 & 2.4) └── cdk/ # Directory containing all AWS CDK infrastructure code in TypeScript Infrastructure source code is completely separated from the backend application source code in the cdk directory, making resource lifecycle management and CI/CD independent and clear.
2. Initialize AWS CDK Project with TypeScript Open Terminal in VS Code (Ctrl + ~) or PowerShell in the root directory IaC-ECS-CDK.
Create the cdk directory and switch into it:
mkdir cdk cd cdk Initialize a new AWS CDK project with the TypeScript template: npx cdk init app --language typescript The cdk init command automatically generates a basic project scaffold with TypeScript file structure, configuration files cdk.json, tsconfig.json, and installs initial packages via npm.
After the initialization command finishes, the structure inside the cdk directory will be:
cdk/ ├── bin/ │ └── cdk.ts # Application entry point for CDK ├── lib/ │ └── cdk-stack.ts # Where AWS resources are defined (CDK Stack) ├── package.json # Defines dependencies and scripts └── tsconfig.json # TypeScript compiler configuration 3. Install CDK Libraries and Constructs AWS CDK v2 groups all service constructs into a single library aws-cdk-lib. Check and install the latest versions of aws-cdk-lib and constructs:
npm install aws-cdk-lib constructs The package.json file in the cdk directory will record the main dependencies.
4. Write Source Code for ECR Stack (cdk-stack.ts) Access /lib and open the cdk-stack.ts file to update the content defining the ECR repository stack:
import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { Construct } from 'constructs'; import * as ecr from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-ecr'; export class CdkStack extends cdk.Stack { public readonly repository: ecr.Repository; constructor(scope: Construct, id: string, props?: cdk.StackProps) { super(scope, id, props); // Create Amazon ECR Repository to store Docker images this.repository = new ecr.Repository(this, 'ProductsServiceRepository', { repositoryName: 'fcaj-products-service', emptyOnDelete: true, removalPolicy: cdk.RemovalPolicy.DESTROY, }); // Output Repository URI after deploy new cdk.CfnOutput(this, 'RepositoryUri', { value: this.repository.repositoryUri, description: 'URI of the ECR repository', }); } } 5. Detailed Explanation of Properties public readonly repository: ecr.Repository;: Declares a public property so that the repository object can be passed to other stacks (for example: EcsStack in later sections will need to reference this repository to pull the image and run it on Fargate Tasks).
repositoryName: ‘fcaj-products-service’: The name of the ECR repository on AWS. This name must be unique within your account and region.
removalPolicy: cdk.RemovalPolicy.DESTROY: Specifies the resource handling policy when the Stack is deleted. By default, CloudFormation retains (RETAIN) storage resources to prevent unintended data loss. In a practice/lab environment, setting DESTROY makes it easy to clean up resources without errors.
emptyOnDelete: true: Automatically deletes all images inside the repository before destroying the repository. Without this option, CloudFormation will fail to delete the repository if it still contains images.
cdk.CfnOutput: Prints the repositoryUri address to the console output immediately after successful deployment, making it easy to copy for tagging and pushing Docker images.

Test project on Postman Create an HTTP GET request to http://localhost:8080/actuator/health to test.
The response returns "status": "UP", indicating that the project is operating normally.
If you encounter an issue where you cannot test HTTP GET with http://localhost:8080/actuator/health, please check the configuration in pom.xml to ensure the spring-boot-starter-actuator dependency has been added. If not, add the library:
<dependency> <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId> <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId> </dependency>

title: Introduction to Architecture and Services
content:
Introduction to Architecture and Services Lab Objectives The objective of this lab is to help learners understand the entire journey from application source code to a running REST service on AWS. We will start with Spring Boot and Docker, then use ECR as the image repository, ECS Fargate as the container runtime, VPC as the private network, DynamoDB as the database, and API Gateway as the public entry point.
What is AWS CDK? AWS Cloud Development Kit, or AWS CDK, is a framework for defining AWS infrastructure using programming languages. In this lab, TypeScript describes the stack and resources. The cdk synth command synthesizes TypeScript into CloudFormation templates, while cdk deploy requests CloudFormation to create or update those resources.
You can think of CDK as an executable blueprint. Instead of manually creating each VPC, subnet, ECS service, or API Gateway in the AWS Management Console, we store the blueprint in source code. When the source code changes, CDK generates a new template version for CloudFormation to compare and deploy.
Repository Directory Structure The repository is divided into two distinct parts:
The fcaj-spring directory contains the application source code and Dockerfile. The cdk directory contains all TypeScript code used to describe AWS infrastructure. IaC-ECS-CDK/ ├─ fcaj-spring/ # Spring Boot and Dockerfile │ ├─ pom.xml # Maven dependencies and configuration │ ├─ Dockerfile # Docker image recipe │ └─ src/main/java/com/example/ │ └─ fcaj_spring/products/ # Product model, controller and AWS config └─ cdk/ # AWS infrastructure in TypeScript ├─ bin/cdk.ts # CDK entrypoint: initializes and connects stacks └─ lib/ ├─ cdk-stack.ts # Creates ECR repository ├─ vpc-stack.ts # Creates VPC and subnets ├─ dynamodb-stack.ts # Creates products table ├─ ecs-stack.ts # ECS, Fargate, task definition and internal ALB ├─ nlb-stack.ts # Internal NLB forwarding to ALB └─ api-gate-way-stack.ts # HTTP API and VPC Link The bin/cdk.ts file is the entry point of the CDK application. This file instantiates stacks and passes resources between them. For example, VpcStack provides the VPC to EcsStack, DynamoDbStack provides the products table to the task role, EcsStack provides the ALB listener to NlbStack, and NlbStack provides the NLB listener to ApiGatewayStack.
When reading the code, you should follow the sequence: bin/cdk.ts, cdk-stack.ts, vpc-stack.ts, dynamodb-stack.ts, ecs-stack.ts, nlb-stack.ts, and api-gate-way-stack.ts. Then switch to fcaj-spring to see how the controller handles requests and how DynamoDbConfig creates the AWS client.
Resources and Their Relationships in the Workshop AWS ECR is the Docker image registry.
AWS ECS is the container orchestration service from AWS, while AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine that runs containers without having to manage EC2 instances -> reducing operational overhead for containerized applications.
AWS VPC provides private network space with public and private subnets.
AWS ALB understands the HTTP protocol and performs health checks against the /actuator/health endpoint of Spring Boot. AWS NLB provides a stable listener for private integration. AWS VPC Link creates a private connection from API Gateway into the VPC. AWS API Gateway receives external requests and forwards them via VPC Link to NLB, ALB, and the ECS tasks.
AWS IAM is a service that provides access control to AWS resources. In this workshop, it includes:
Task execution role: pull image from ECR and send logs to CloudWatch. Task role: for the Spring Boot application to call DynamoDB and X-Ray. AWS DynamoDB is a powerful non-relational NoSQL database management service. This lab introduces the use of DynamoDB Enhanced Client from AWS SDK v2 for Java, a high-level library that maps client-side classes to DynamoDB tables.
AWS CloudWatch Logs centralizes container and application logs. The applications created in this course write logs to CloudWatch Logs in JSON format using the Log4j2 library. This allows inserting parameters into logs to be used in queries within the AWS CloudWatch Logs Insights console.
The AWS X-Ray daemon sidecar collects, batches, and sends trace data (request traces) from the application container to the AWS X-Ray service over the internal network (UDP).
Request Processing Flow When a user calls GET /api/products, the request reaches API Gateway. API Gateway forwards the request through the VPC Link to the NLB listener. NLB forwards it to the internal ALB. ALB selects a healthy ECS task based on health checks. Spring Boot processes the request, queries DynamoDB, and returns the response. Logs are sent to CloudWatch, while traces are sent to the X-Ray daemon running alongside the application container.
Because the ALB is internal (inside private subnet), internet users cannot call the ALB DNS directly. This is why the lab places API Gateway and VPC Link in front.

title: Create Controller, Model and Configure DynamoDB, X-Ray
content:
1. Create Model and Controller for Product Create the products folder and create the Product.java file. Copy the following code: import software.amazon.awssdk.enhanced.dynamodb.mapper.annotations.DynamoDbBean; import software.amazon.awssdk.enhanced.dynamodb.mapper.annotations.DynamoDbPartitionKey; @DynamoDbBean public class Product { private String id; private String name; private Double price; public Product() {} public Product(String id, String name, Double price) { this.id = id; this.name = name; this.price = price; } @DynamoDbPartitionKey public String getId() { return id; } public void setId(String id) { this.id = id; } public String getName() { return name; } public void setName(String name) { this.name = name; } public Double getPrice() { return price; } public void setPrice(Double price) { this.price = price; } } Create the ProductController.java file. Copy the following code: import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.List; import org.apache.logging.log4j.LogManager; import org.apache.logging.log4j.Logger; import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.DeleteMapping; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PutMapping; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController; import software.amazon.awssdk.enhanced.dynamodb.DynamoDbEnhancedClient; import software.amazon.awssdk.enhanced.dynamodb.DynamoDbTable; import software.amazon.awssdk.enhanced.dynamodb.Key; import software.amazon.awssdk.enhanced.dynamodb.TableSchema; @RestController @RequestMapping("/api/products") public class ProductController { private static final Logger LOG = LogManager.getLogger(ProductController.class); private final DynamoDbTable<Product> productTable; public ProductController(DynamoDbEnhancedClient enhancedClient) { this.productTable = enhancedClient.table("products", TableSchema.fromBean(Product.class)); } @GetMapping public List<Product> getAllProducts() { LOG.info("Fetching all products from DynamoDB"); List<Product> products = new ArrayList<>(); productTable.scan().items().forEach(products::add); return products; } @GetMapping("/{id}") public ResponseEntity<Product> getProductById(@PathVariable String id) { LOG.info("Fetching product: {}", id); Product product = productTable.getItem(Key.builder().partitionValue(id).build()); return product != null ? ResponseEntity.ok(product) : ResponseEntity.notFound().build(); } @PostMapping public List<Product> createProduct(@RequestBody List<Product> products) { for (Product product : products) { LOG.info("Creating product: {}", product.getId()); productTable.putItem(product); } return products; } @PutMapping public Product updateProduct(@RequestBody Product product) { LOG.info("Updating product: {}", product.getId()); productTable.updateItem(product); return product; } @DeleteMapping("/{id}") public ResponseEntity<Void> deleteProduct(@PathVariable String id) { LOG.info("Deleting product: {}", id); productTable.deleteItem(Key.builder().partitionValue(id).build()); return ResponseEntity.noContent().build(); } } 2. Configure DynamoDB and AWS X-Ray Create the DynamoDbConfig.java file (Client configuration with X-Ray Interceptor). Copy the following code: import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean; import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration; import com.amazonaws.xray.interceptors.TracingInterceptor; import software.amazon.awssdk.enhanced.dynamodb.DynamoDbEnhancedClient; import software.amazon.awssdk.services.dynamodb.DynamoDbClient; @Configuration public class DynamoDbConfig { @Bean public DynamoDbClient dynamoDbClient() { return DynamoDbClient.builder() .overrideConfiguration(builder -> builder.addExecutionInterceptor(new TracingInterceptor())) .build(); } @Bean public DynamoDbEnhancedClient dynamoDbEnhancedClient(DynamoDbClient dynamoDbClient) { return DynamoDbEnhancedClient.builder() .dynamoDbClient(dynamoDbClient) .build(); } } Create the WebConfig.java file (X-Ray Tracing Servlet Filter following Jakarta EE standard). Copy the following code: import com.amazonaws.xray.AWSXRay; import com.amazonaws.xray.entities.Segment; import jakarta.servlet.*; import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest; import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse; import org.springframework.boot.web.servlet.FilterRegistrationBean; import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean; import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration; import org.springframework.core.Ordered; import java.io.IOException; import java.util.HashMap; import java.util.Map; @Configuration public class WebConfig { @Bean public FilterRegistrationBean<Filter> tracingFilter() { FilterRegistrationBean<Filter> registration = new FilterRegistrationBean<>(); registration.setFilter(new Filter() { @Override public void doFilter(ServletRequest request, ServletResponse response, FilterChain chain) throws IOException, ServletException { HttpServletRequest req = (HttpServletRequest) request; HttpServletResponse res = (HttpServletResponse) response; // Start X-Ray segment for the service Segment segment = AWSXRay.beginSegment("fcaj-products-service"); try { chain.doFilter(request, response); if (segment != null) { int status = res.getStatus(); Map<String, Object> responseAttributes = new HashMap<>(); responseAttributes.put("status", status); segment.putHttp("response", responseAttributes); if (status >= 400 && status < 500) { segment.setError(true); } else if (status >= 500) { segment.setFault(true); } } } catch (Exception e) { if (segment != null) { segment.addException(e); segment.setFault(true); } throw e; } finally { AWSXRay.endSegment(); } } }); registration.addUrlPatterns("/*"); registration.setOrder(Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE); return registration; } } If you encounter issues during the Spring Boot build process (inline errors or dependency conflicts), please check:
Duplicate dependencies: .\mvnw dependency:tree: This command lists the dependency tree to help check for duplicate or conflicting dependencies. Local cache issues: often caused by local cache or classpath conflicts. Try running: .\mvnw clean compile: This command clears the local build cache and recompiles. Restart VS Code. You have completed creating the Spring Boot Product Service (ECR). The files include configurations for AWS X-Ray and DynamoDB.

title: Create Network Load Balancer and deploy Stack
content:
After defining EcsStack, the next step is to build the Network Load Balancer (NLB) placed in front of the ALB to act as the reception point for the API Gateway VPC Link in subsequent steps, interconnect the Stacks in bin/cdk.ts, and proceed with deployment to AWS.
1. Role of Network Load Balancer in the Architecture In the enterprise-grade secure microservices architecture on AWS:
ALB operates at the application layer (Layer 7), responsible for HTTP path routing and managing Spring Boot application health checks. NLB operates at the transport layer (Layer 4), providing extreme performance, ultra-low latency, and acting as an ideal target for VPC Link from API Gateway into the private network. By combining NLB -> ALB -> ECS Fargate, the system optimizes private connection performance while taking full advantage of the rich routing capabilities of the Application Load Balancer. 2. Write NLB Stack Source Code (nlb-stack.ts) Navigate to the directory IaC-ECS-CDK/cdk/lib and open the file nlb-stack.ts (or create it if not present). Update the contents defining NlbStack:
import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { Construct } from 'constructs'; import * as ec2 from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-ec2'; import * as elbv2 from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-elasticloadbalancingv2'; import * as targets from 'aws-cdk-lib/aws-elasticloadbalancingv2-targets'; interface NlbStackProps extends cdk.StackProps { vpc: ec2.IVpc; albListener: elbv2.ApplicationListener; } export class NlbStack extends cdk.Stack { public readonly nlb: elbv2.NetworkLoadBalancer; public readonly listener: elbv2.NetworkListener; constructor(scope: Construct, id: string, props: NlbStackProps) { super(scope, id, props); // 1. Create explicit Security Group for NLB const nlbSecurityGroup = new ec2.SecurityGroup(this, 'NlbSecurityGroup', { vpc: props.vpc, description: 'Security group for internal Network Load Balancer', allowAllOutbound: true, // Allow NLB to send health check and traffic to ALB }); // Open port 80 allowing the entire VPC network range to connect (API Gateway VPC Link) nlbSecurityGroup.addIngressRule( ec2.Peer.ipv4(props.vpc.vpcCidrBlock), ec2.Port.tcp(80), 'Allow HTTP from VPC (API Gateway VPC Link)' ); // 2. Initialize internal NLB and assign explicit Security Group this.nlb = new elbv2.NetworkLoadBalancer(this, 'InternalNlb', { vpc: props.vpc, internetFacing: false, // Internal NLB securityGroups: [nlbSecurityGroup], vpcSubnets: { subnetType: ec2.SubnetType.PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS, }, }); // 3. Add port 80 Listener for NLB this.listener = this.nlb.addListener('NlbListener', { port: 80, }); // 4. Forward requests from NLB to Application Load Balancer Listener this.listener.addTargets('NlbToAlbTargets', { port: 80, targets: [new targets.AlbListenerTarget(props.albListener)], healthCheck: { protocol: elbv2.Protocol.HTTP, port: '80', path: '/actuator/health', healthyHttpCodes: '200', }, }); } } 3. Organize and Connect Stacks in bin/cdk.ts Open the file bin/cdk.ts in VS Code to register and connect the Stacks together:
#!/usr/bin/env node import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { CdkStack } from '../lib/cdk-stack'; import { VpcStack } from '../lib/vpc-stack'; import { EcsStack } from '../lib/ecs-stack'; import { DynamoDbStack } from '../lib/dynamodb-stack'; import { NlbStack } from '../lib/nlb-stack'; const app = new cdk.App(); const env: cdk.Environment = { account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT, region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION ?? 'ap-southeast-1', }; // 1. ECR Stack const ecrStack = new CdkStack(app, 'ProductsServiceEcrStack', { env }); // 2. VPC Stack const vpcStack = new VpcStack(app, 'ProductsServiceVpcStack', { env }); // 3. DynamoDB Stack const dynamoStack = new DynamoDbStack(app, 'ProductsServiceDynamoDbStack', { env }); // 4. ECS Fargate Stack (Receives parameters from VPC, DynamoDB, and ECR) const ecsStack = new EcsStack(app, 'ProductsServiceEcsStack', { env, vpc: vpcStack.vpc, table: dynamoStack.table, repository: ecrStack.repository, }); // 5. NLB Stack (Receives VPC and listener from ECS Stack) const nlbStack = new NlbStack(app, 'ProductsServiceNlbStack', { env, vpc: vpcStack.vpc, albListener: ecsStack.albListener, }); 4. Compile and Check Source Code Run the build command to check TypeScript syntax errors: npm run build Check the list of registered Stacks: npx cdk list or
cdk list 5. Deploy Stacks to AWS (cdk deploy) Run the command to deploy all necessary stacks simultaneously:
npx cdk deploy ProductsServiceDynamoDbStack ProductsServiceEcsStack ProductsServiceNlbStack --require-approval never AWS CDK will automatically analyze the dependency graph to deploy in the correct order: DynamoDB -> ECS Fargate -> NLB. This process typically takes about 3 to 5 minutes to launch the Fargate cluster and configure the Load Balancers.
6. Check Resources on AWS Management Console Check CloudFormation has successfully created ecs, dynamodb, nlb stacks. 1. Check Amazon ECS Cluster and Service Sign in to the AWS Management Console > select Elastic Container Service (ECS). Click on the cluster fcaj-products-cluster. Under the Services tab, you will see the service fcaj-products-service with status Active and Running tasks: 1/1. Switch to the Tasks / Task definitions tab and click on the running Task. Check the Containers section: Container web: Runs the Spring Boot image, port 8080. Container xray-daemon: Runs the X-Ray sidecar, port 2000 UDP. 2. Check Load Balancers (ALB and NLB) Go to the EC2 service > select Load Balancers from the left menu. You will see 2 internal load balancers:
InternalAlb: Type application, scheme internal. InternalNlb: Type network, scheme internal. 3. Check Target Groups and Health Check Go to the Target groups section in the left menu:
Select the Target Group of Internal ALB (port 8080) > check the Targets tab: Status of the Fargate Task is Healthy (passed the health check /actuator/health). Select the Target Group of Internal NLB (port 80) > check the Targets tab: Status of the ALB target is Healthy. In case of encountering unhealthy error on port 80 of the target group In case of encountering an unhealthy error on port 80 of the target group, you need to check and ensure the security group of the NLB has the following inbound and outbound rules:
inbound rules: Type: HTTP, Port: 80, Source: 0.0.0.0/0 outbound rules: All traffic, Destination: Anywhere-IPv4 (0.0.0.0/0) (or specify the VPC CIDR range 10.0.0.0/16) Congratulations! You have completed deploying the Spring Boot application running on the serverless Amazon ECS Fargate cluster with 2 containers (App + X-Ray Daemon), securely connected via Internal Application Load Balancer and Network Load Balancer. This infrastructure is ready to integrate with API Gateway in step 7!

title: Environment preparation
content:
Environment preparation All installation and verification steps prior to creating AWS resources are located in this section. The goal is to confirm that the local machine can build Spring Boot, run Docker containers, and synthesize CDK before deploying.
The lab uses region ap-southeast-1. If you choose another region, you need to change the region in AWS CLI commands, in the CDK configuration, and in the Spring Boot application.
Preparation Steps Below is the step-by-step guide to installing the required tools from their official websites and verifying their versions in the Terminal.
1. Java Development Kit (JDK 25)
Official Download Page: Oracle Java Downloads or Adoptium Eclipse Temurin Steps: Access the download link and select the installer suitable for your operating system (e.g., Windows x64 Installer .exe / .msi, macOS .pkg, or Linux .tar.gz). Open the downloaded file and proceed with the installation using default settings. Ensure the JAVA_HOME environment variable is configured and the path %JAVA_HOME%\bin is added to the system PATH variable. Verify version in Terminal / PowerShell: java -version javac -version Output: java version "25" ... Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment ... javac 25 2. Node.js (LTS v24.x) and npm (v11)
Official Download Page: Node.js Official Download Steps: Visit the Node.js homepage and download the LTS installer (version v24.x). Run the installer (.msi on Windows or .pkg on macOS), click Next, and accept default terms to complete. Verify version in Terminal / PowerShell: node -v npm -v Sample Output: v24.x.x 11.x.x 3. AWS CLI
Official Download Page: AWS CLI Installation Guide | Direct Download AWS CLI for Windows (MSI) Steps: Download the AWS CLI v2 installation package corresponding to your operating system. Launch the installer and follow the on-screen instructions. Restart your Terminal / PowerShell window to reload new environment variables. Verify version in Terminal / PowerShell: aws --version Sample Output: aws-cli/2.x.x Python/3.x.x Windows/10 exe/x86_64 4. AWS CDK
Official Documentation Page: AWS CDK Documentation | AWS CDK on npm Steps: Install AWS CDK globally via npm: npm install -g aws-cdk Verify version in Terminal / PowerShell: cdk --version Sample Output: 2.x.x (build ...) 5. Install Postman
Official Download Page: Postman Download Steps: Go to the link and download the Postman Desktop Agent / App suitable for your operating system. Launch the installer file to open the Postman application. Sign in or select Skip and go to the app to be ready to send test API requests after the Spring Boot application is deployed. 6. Install VS Code and Extensions for Spring Boot
Official Download Page: Visual Studio Code Download
Steps:
Download and install VS Code. Open VS Code, press Ctrl + Shift + X (on Windows/Linux) or Cmd + Shift + X (on macOS) to open the Extensions panel. Search and install the following extensions: Extension Pack for Java (vscjava.vscode-java-pack) Language Support for Java™ by Red Hat (redhat.java) Spring Boot Extension Pack (vmware.vscode-boot-dev-pack) Spring Initializr Java Support (vscjava.vscode-spring-initializr) Docker (ms-azuretools.vscode-docker) Docker DX (docker.docker) AWS Toolkit (amazonwebservices.aws-toolkit-vscode) (Optional) You can quickly install all extensions via Terminal command:
code --install-extension vscjava.vscode-java-pack code --install-extension redhat.java code --install-extension vmware.vscode-boot-dev-pack code --install-extension vscjava.vscode-spring-initializr Verify installation in Terminal / PowerShell:
code --version code --list-extensions 7. Install Docker Desktop
Official Download Page: Docker Desktop Download Steps: Download the Docker Desktop installation package suitable for your operating system (on Windows, enabling the WSL 2 backend feature is recommended). Proceed with the installation and restart your computer if required. Launch Docker Desktop and make sure the displayed status is Engine running. Verify version and status in Terminal / PowerShell: docker --version docker compose version docker info Sample Output: Docker version 29.x.x, build ... Docker Compose version v5.x.x Docker Desktop Troubleshooting (WSL 2 & Virtualization on Windows):
If Docker Desktop fails to launch or displays errors regarding WSL 2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux), “WSL 2 installation is incomplete”, or “Virtualization is not enabled in BIOS”, follow these steps:
Step 1: Check Virtualization Features in Control Panel Press the Windows key, search for and open Turn Windows features on or off (or navigate to Control Panel > Programs and Features > Turn Windows features on or off). Ensure the following features are checked: Virtual Machine Platform Windows Hypervisor Platform Windows Subsystem for Linux (Optional for Hyper-V): Hyper-V Click OK to apply the features. Step 2: Check and Install WSL 2 via PowerShell (Administrator) Open PowerShell as an administrator (Run as Administrator):
Verify if WSL is installed on your system:
wsl --status If version details and kernel version appear, WSL is already installed. If an error like wsl is not recognized... appears or WSL is disabled: Enable Virtualization and Install WSL: Enable Hyper-V:
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Microsoft-Hyper-V -All Install the latest WSL:
wsl --install (Or install WSL without default Linux distribution if used exclusively for Docker: wsl --install --no-distribution).
Update the WSL kernel to the latest version:
wsl --update Set WSL 2 as the default version for Docker:
wsl --set-default-version 2 Restart your computer so that all virtualization features and the WSL kernel take effect.
Step 3: Verify Stable WSL Status After restarting, open PowerShell again and verify the WSL status:
Check WSL configuration status:
wsl --status Expected output confirming a stable WSL 2 environment: Default Version: 2 WSL version: 2.x.x Kernel version: 5.x.x (or newer) WSLg version: ... Check the list of running Linux distributions for Docker:
wsl -l -v When Docker Desktop runs successfully, you will see backend processes in the Running state on version 2: NAME STATE VERSION * docker-desktop Running 2 docker-desktop-data Running 2 Launch the Docker Desktop application; the Docker whale icon in your system tray should turn green (Engine running).

title: Organize and deploy API Gateway Stack
content:
After completing the source code for ApiGatewayStack in the lib directory, the next step is to declare this stack in the main entry point bin/cdk.ts, compile and check the source code, deploy to AWS, and perform end-to-end testing from the outside via the Internet.
1. Register and Link Stacks in bin/cdk.ts Open the file IaC-ECS-CDK/cdk/bin/cdk.ts in VS Code. Ensure the entire chain of 6 Stacks is connected sequentially according to the dependency tree:
#!/usr/bin/env node import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { CdkStack } from '../lib/cdk-stack'; import { VpcStack } from '../lib/vpc-stack'; import { DynamoDbStack } from '../lib/dynamodb-stack'; import { EcsStack } from '../lib/ecs-stack'; import { NlbStack } from '../lib/nlb-stack'; import { ApiGatewayStack } from '../lib/api-gate-way-stack'; const app = new cdk.App(); const env: cdk.Environment = { account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT, region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION ?? 'ap-southeast-1', }; // 1. ECR Stack const ecrStack = new CdkStack(app, 'ProductsServiceEcrStack', { env }); // 2. VPC Stack const vpcStack = new VpcStack(app, 'ProductsServiceVpcStack', { env }); // 3. DynamoDB Stack const dynamoStack = new DynamoDbStack(app, 'ProductsServiceDynamoDbStack', { env }); // 4. ECS Fargate Stack (Receives VPC, DynamoDB Table and ECR Repo) const ecsStack = new EcsStack(app, 'ProductsServiceEcsStack', { env, vpc: vpcStack.vpc, table: dynamoStack.table, repository: ecrStack.repository, }); // 5. NLB Stack (Receives VPC and ALB Listener from ecsStack) const nlbStack = new NlbStack(app, 'ProductsServiceNlbStack', { env, vpc: vpcStack.vpc, albListener: ecsStack.albListener, }); // 6. API Gateway Stack (Receives VPC and NLB Listener from nlbStack) new ApiGatewayStack(app, 'ProductsServiceApiGatewayStack', { env, vpc: vpcStack.vpc, nlbListener: nlbStack.listener, }); 2. Compile and Check Source Code Run the TypeScript build command to check the validity of all source code: npm run build List all registered Stacks: npx cdk list or:
cdk list Synthesize and inspect the CloudFormation template for the API Gateway Stack: npx cdk synth ProductsServiceApiGatewayStack 3. Deploy API Gateway Stack to AWS (cdk deploy) Run the command to deploy only ProductsServiceApiGatewayStack:
npx cdk deploy ProductsServiceApiGatewayStack --require-approval never Deploying the API Gateway typically takes about 2 to 3 minutes. This time is mainly spent by AWS allocating the Network Interfaces (ENI) of the VPC Link attached to the Private Subnets in your VPC.
When deployment completes, the terminal will print the public Invoke URL of API Gateway.
4. Check Resources on AWS Management Console Check CloudFormation ProductsServiceApiGatewayStack created successfully. Sign in to the AWS Management Console > Select the CloudFormation service. Check HTTP API Gateway and VPC Link Select the API Gateway service. Click on the API fcaj-products-api-enterprise (Type HTTP). In the left menu, select VPC links: Verify link HttpVpcLink is in the Available state and linked to the correct VPC ID of the lab. Switch to Routes: You will see the route ANY /{proxy+} automatically created and linked with integration NlbIntegration pointing to the listener of the Network Load Balancer. Switch to Metrics: Enable Detailed route metrics to allow tracking detailed metrics for each route. 5. Comprehensive End-to-End System Testing from the Internet Now you can open a terminal (PowerShell, Git Bash, or Command Prompt) on your personal computer or use Postman to call the APIs:
1. Check Actuator Health Check Endpoint Send a request to check the health of the Spring Boot application:
https://<api-id>.execute-api.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com/actuator/health (Replace <api-id> with the actual API Gateway ID displayed in the Outputs section)
Expected result returns HTTP status 200 OK:
{"status":"UP"} If you receive {"status":"UP"}, congratulations! The request from your personal computer successfully traveled through the Internet -> API Gateway -> VPC Link -> Internal NLB -> Internal ALB -> Spring Boot Container in ECS Fargate.
2. Create a new product in DynamoDB (POST) Send a POST request with JSON-formatted product data:
Open Postman -> Body -> Method: Post
Paste the URL with the API Gateway endpoint:
https://<api-id>.execute-api.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com/api/products Select Body -> raw [ { "id": "1", "name": "Asus Zephyrus 16 duo", "price": 160000.0 }, { "id": "2", "name": "Alienware Area 51", "price": 999999.0 }, { "id": "3", "name": "Razer Blade 16", "price": 900000.0 } ] 4. Verify data on DynamoDB Console and GET by ID Call the GET request for the product list again: https://<apigw-id>.execute-api.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com/api/products Now the API will return the list containing the newly created products.
Access DynamoDB Console -> Explore items: You will see the new product records appear directly in the table with string partition key id and associated fields. Congratulations on completing the entire Enterprise-standard secure Microservices architecture on AWS using AWS CDK! The entire infrastructure from Private network, NoSQL database, serverless Fargate compute cluster, 2-layer load balancing (NLB + ALB) to API Gateway operates harmoniously and with absolute security.

title: Organize and deploy DynamoDB Stack
content:
After completing the source code for DynamoDbStack in the lib directory, the next step is to declare the stack in the main entry point file bin/cdk.ts, check TypeScript compilation, and deploy the products table to AWS.
1. Declare DynamoDB Stack in bin/cdk.ts Open the file IaC-ECS-CDK/cdk/bin/cdk.ts in VS Code and add the declaration to initialize DynamoDbStack:
#!/usr/bin/env node import 'source-map-support/register'; import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { EcrStack } from '../lib/ecr-stack'; import { VpcStack } from '../lib/vpc-stack'; import { DynamoDbStack } from '../lib/dynamodb-stack'; const app = new cdk.App(); const env: cdk.Environment = { account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT, region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION || 'ap-southeast-1', }; // 1. VPC Stack const vpcStack = new VpcStack(app, 'ProductsServiceVpcStack', { env }); // 2. ECR Stack const ecrStack = new EcrStack(app, 'ProductsServiceEcrStack', { env }); // 3. DynamoDB Stack const dynamoStack = new DynamoDbStack(app, 'ProductsServiceDynamoDbStack', { env }); Note: The dynamoStack object provides the property dynamoStack.table (type dynamodb.Table). In the next step, this object will be passed directly into ProductsServiceEcsStack to grant IAM read/write permissions to the ECS Fargate container.
2. Compile and Check Source Code List the Stacks registered in the CDK application: npx cdk list Output displayed on the terminal:
Synthesize and inspect the standard CloudFormation Template for the DynamoDB stack: npx cdk synth ProductsServiceDynamoDbStack The above command synthesizes a pure CloudFormation template containing the AWS::DynamoDB::Table resource with the Partition Key and On-Demand Billing configurations that we defined.
3. Deploy DynamoDB Stack to AWS (cdk deploy) Run the command to deploy only ProductsServiceDynamoDbStack:
npx cdk deploy ProductsServiceDynamoDbStack --require-approval never Since DynamoDB is a purely serverless service, AWS does not need to provision physical hardware or complex VPC networking. Table creation occurs very quickly, typically taking only 30 to 45 seconds to complete.
4. Check Resources on AWS Management Console Access CloudFormation, check ProductsServiceDynamoDbStack successfully created Sign in to the AWS Management Console. Access the CloudFormation service. In the search bar, type DynamoDB and click the service. In the left navigation bar, select Tables. Click on the table name products in the list to view details: Table status: Active (Table is ready for operations). Partition key: id (String). Capacity mode: On-demand (Pay per request). Great! The products database table has been successfully created on AWS. In Step 6, we will build the Amazon ECS Fargate cluster, grant DynamoDB read/write permissions to the Task Role, and deploy the entire Spring Boot application along with the ALB/NLB load balancing system.

title: Organize and deploy VPC stack using AWS CDK
content:
After defining VpcStack in the lib directory, the next step is to declare and organize this Stack in the main entry point at bin/cdk.ts, compile and check the source code, and deploy the network infrastructure to AWS.
1. Organize VPC Stack in bin/cdk.ts Navigate to the bin directory and open the cdk.ts file in VS Code. Add the initialization declaration for VpcStack:
#!/usr/bin/env node import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { CdkStack } from '../lib/cdk-stack'; import { VpcStack } from '../lib/vpc-stack'; const app = new cdk.App(); const env: cdk.Environment = { account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT, region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION ?? 'ap-southeast-1', }; // Initialize ECR Stack const ecrStack = new CdkStack(app, 'ProductsServiceEcrStack', { env }); // Initialize VPC Stack const vpcStack = new VpcStack(app, 'ProductsServiceVpcStack', { env, }); Note: The vpcStack object will later be used to pass network attributes vpc: vpcStack.vpc into the ECS Fargate cluster and Internal Load Balancers in subsequent steps.
2. Compile and Check Source Code Run the build command for the TypeScript compiler (tsc) to check all syntax errors: npm run build Check the list of Stacks registered in the CDK App: npx cdk list Or:
cdk list Output displayed:
ProductsServiceEcrStack ProductsServiceVpcStack Synthesize and inspect the standard CloudFormation Template for the VPC Stack: npx cdk synth ProductsServiceVpcStack 3. Deploy VPC Stack to AWS (cdk deploy) Open Terminal in VS Code at the IaC-ECS-CDK/cdk directory.
Run the command to deploy only the VPC Stack:
npx cdk deploy ProductsServiceVpcStack --require-approval never The process of creating the VPC, allocating Elastic IP, and configuring the NAT Gateway usually takes about 2 to 3 minutes. The CDK CLI will update resource creation progress in real time on the terminal screen.
4. Check Resources on AWS Management Console 1. Check CloudFormation Stack Sign in to the AWS Management Console. Search for the CloudFormation service (ensure the correct Region ap-southeast-1 is selected). You will see the ProductsServiceVpcStack stack with the status CREATE_COMPLETE. 2. Check VPC Go to the VPC service > select Your VPCs. You will see the VPC named ecs-cdk-vpc with default IPv4 CIDR range 10.0.0.0/16.
3. Check Subnets Go to the Subnets section in the left menu. The system has automatically created 4 subnets across 2 AZs:
2 Public Subnets (1 subnet per AZ): ProductsServiceVpcStack/VpcLab/PublicSubnetSubnet1 and ...Subnet2. 2 Private Subnets (1 subnet per AZ): ProductsServiceVpcStack/VpcLab/PrivateSubnetSubnet1 and ...Subnet2. 4. Check NAT Gateway Go to the NAT gateways section in the left menu. You will see 1 NAT Gateway in the Available state, allocated an Elastic IP, and placed in the Public Subnet.
5. Check Route Tables Go to the Route tables section in the left menu to inspect routing configuration:
Public Route Table: Has route 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to the Internet Gateway (igw-xxxxxx). Private Route Table: Has route 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to the NAT Gateway (nat-xxxxxx), ensuring containers running in the Private Subnet have one-way outbound Internet access. Congratulations! You have completed building and deploying a secure standard VPC network infrastructure with AWS CDK. This network system is ready to host the Amazon ECS Fargate cluster and database in the following lessons.

title: Organize CDK Stack in CDK project
content:
After defining CdkStack for ECR in the lib directory, the next step is to declare and organize this Stack in the application’s main entry point at bin/cdk.ts, configure the deployment environment (AWS Account & Region), and verify the correctness of the source code before deploying.
1. Configure Entry Point (cdk.ts) Access bin and open the cdk.ts file in VS Code. This file acts as the “conductor” to initialize the CDK application ( cdk.App ) and connect Stacks together.
Update the contents of bin/cdk.ts to initialize ProductsServiceEcrStack:
#!/usr/bin/env node import * as cdk from 'aws-cdk-lib'; import { CdkStack } from '../lib/cdk-stack'; const app = new cdk.App(); // Configure the deployment environment with information retrieved from AWS CLI const env: cdk.Environment = { account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT, region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION ?? 'ap-southeast-1', }; // Initialize ECR Stack with a clear stack name const ecrStack = new CdkStack(app, 'ProductsServiceEcrStack', { env }); Important Points Explained: env: Object determining the target AWS account and region where the infrastructure will be created.
process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT: CDK automatically reads the currently logged-in Account ID from the AWS CLI (aws sts get-caller-identity).
process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION ?? ‘ap-southeast-1’: Sets Singapore (ap-southeast-1) as the default region.
ProductsServiceEcrStack: This is the unique identifier of the CloudFormation Stack when created on AWS. Giving it a descriptive prefix makes it easy to distinguish from other stacks in the same lab.
2. Compile and Check TypeScript Errors Whenever you edit TypeScript code, you should run the build command so the tsc compiler can check syntax and data types:
npm run build If the command finishes without any error messages in the terminal, your TypeScript code is completely valid and was compiled successfully.
3. Check Stack List (cdk list) Run the cdk list command to check the list of Stacks registered in the CDK application:
npx cdk list Or:
cdk list This confirms that CDK has properly recognized the ProductsServiceEcrStack Stack and it is ready for deployment.
4. Synthesize CloudFormation Template (cdk synth) The synth (synthesize) command translates all TypeScript code into equivalent CloudFormation templates (in JSON/YAML format) and stores them in the cdk.out directory:
npx cdk synth ProductsServiceEcrStack Note: The npx cdk synth command only executes in your local environment to generate and validate CloudFormation templates; it does not create any resources on AWS yet. This helps you catch configuration errors early before submitting requests to the cloud.
