title: Create ECR Image Repository with AWS CDK and push Docker image
content: Create ECR and push the Docker image In this section, we will learn how to provision an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) repository on AWS using AWS CDK (TypeScript). We will also authenticate Docker CLI, tag, and push our Spring Boot container image to the created ECR repository.

title: Create Spring Boot Product Service
content:
To deploy AWS resources in the Cloud (ECR, ECS, DynamoDB, APIs, etc.), we will use the AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK). CDK allows you to define infrastructure using code and automatically generates CloudFormation templates for deployment.
This workshop uses Java Spring Boot for the backend application (ECR) and TypeScript for ECS, VPC, DynamoDB, APIs, etc. You can also build it using Python or other programming languages.
Repository Directory Structure The repository is divided into two distinct parts:
The fcaj-spring directory contains the application source code and Dockerfile. The cdk directory contains all TypeScript code used to describe AWS infrastructure. IaC-ECS-CDK/ ├─ fcaj-spring/ # Spring Boot and Dockerfile │ ├─ pom.xml # Maven dependencies and configuration │ ├─ Dockerfile # Docker image recipe │ └─ src/main/java/com/example/ │ └─ fcaj_spring/products/ # Product model, controller, and AWS config └─ cdk/ # AWS infrastructure in TypeScript ├─ bin/cdk.ts # Stacks initialization and connection └─ lib/ ├─ cdk-stack.ts # Creates ECR repository ├─ vpc-stack.ts # Creates VPC and subnets ├─ dynamodb-stack.ts # Creates products table ├─ ecs-stack.ts # ECS, Fargate, task, and internal ALB ├─ nlb-stack.ts # Internal NLB forwarding to ALB └─ api-gate-way-stack.ts # HTTP API and VPC Link

title: Deploy Stack to AWS ECR
content:
In this step, we will deploy the ProductsServiceEcrStack to our AWS account using the AWS CDK CLI, monitor the CloudFormation resource creation process, and verify the ECR repository in the AWS Management Console.
1. Check Environment Bootstrap Before any stack can be deployed, the AWS environment (Account & Region) must be bootstrapped with management resources (S3 bucket for assets, CDK IAM roles).
Check account information:
aws sts get-caller-identity --output text Run the bootstrap command:
npx cdk bootstrap Access CloudFormation to check the CDKToolkit stack. Access the AWS Console -> CloudFormation -> Stacks -> Select stack CDKToolkit.
2. Deploy ECR Stack (cdk deploy) Open Terminal in VS Code at the IaC-ECS-CDK/cdk directory.
Run the command to deploy only the ECR Stack:
npx cdk deploy ProductsServiceEcrStack --require-approval never Parameter meaning:
The –require-approval never parameter directs CDK to automatically approve security-related changes (such as IAM Roles or Resource Policies) without stopping to ask the user to type y/n, allowing the deployment process to run smoothly.
The deployment process will create a CloudFormation ChangeSet and provision the AWS::ECR::Repository resource. When completed, the terminal will display a success message along with the Outputs information: Save the RepositoryUri value displayed in the Outputs section. This is the unique registry identifier on AWS ECR, which will be used for tagging and pushing the Docker image in the next step.
Access CloudFormation to check the ProductsServiceEcrStack. 3. Verify ECR in the AWS Management Console Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
In the top search bar, type ECR and select the Elastic Container Registry service. Ensure you have selected the correct region Singapore (ap-southeast-1) in the upper right corner.
In the left navigation menu, select Repositories (under Private registry). You will see the newly created repository named fcaj-products-service appear in the list. Click on the repository name fcaj-products-service to view details. Currently, the repository is newly created, so there are no images yet. We will proceed to authenticate Docker and push the image to this repository in the next step.

title: Create Dockerfile and Build Docker Image
content:
The Dockerfile is the recipe for creating an image. In the current file, EXPOSE 8080 describes the application port and ENTRYPOINT starts the Spring Boot class. The Docker image should be built for linux/amd64 to match the Fargate x86_64 environment.
The current Dockerfile copies the target/dependency/BOOT-INF and target/dependency/META-INF directories. If these directories do not exist after the Maven build, docker build will fail. To make the lab accessible, you can use a direct-JAR Dockerfile after aligning the JAR file name with pom.xml. Do not proceed to ECR before running the container locally.
2.4.1 Create Dockerfile and Docker Image 1. Create a .dockerignore file to specify files and directories that Docker will ignore when packaging (building) a Docker image from the project components.
In the project root directory in VS Code, create a file named .dockerignore with the following content: .git .gitignore .dockerignore .vscode *.class README.md 2. Build JAR file and extract
Open Terminal in VS Code (Ctrl + ~), navigate to the .../fcaj-spring directory and run the following commands:
Build the jar file with Maven: .\mvnw.cmd clean package -DskipTests Extract the JAR file into the target/dependency directory: mkdir -Force target\dependency tar -xf (Get-Item target\*.jar).FullName -C target\dependency Verification: Inside the target/dependency/ folder, 3 subdirectories will appear: BOOT-INF, META-INF, and org
3. Create Dockerfile
In the root directory of the project, create a file named Dockerfile (without any extension).
The variable DEPENDENCY = target/dependency points to the directory containing Maven’s extracted build artifacts:
FROM eclipse-temurin:25-jdk-alpine VOLUME /tmp ARG DEPENDENCY=target/dependency COPY ${DEPENDENCY}/BOOT-INF/lib /app/lib COPY ${DEPENDENCY}/META-INF /app/META-INF COPY ${DEPENDENCY}/BOOT-INF/classes /app EXPOSE 8080 ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-cp", "app:app/lib/*", "com.example.fcaj_spring.FcajSpringApplication"] Important notes:
EXPOSE: port 8080 based on the server port configured in application.properties. ENTRYPOINT: main startup class is com.example.fcaj_spring.FcajSpringApplication. 4. Build Docker Image in VS Code Terminal Ensure Docker Desktop is running, then execute the following command in the VS Code terminal:
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t productsservice:1.0.0 . Note the dot . at the end of the command representing the build context in the current directory.
You can also observe this via the Docker extension in VS Code. We have created an image named productsservice with tag 1.0.0. 5. Check Docker Image
Once the terminal finishes building, check the newly created image using the command: docker images 2.4.2 Run Docker Image on Local Machine In this step, we will run a Docker container from the newly built productsservice:1.0.0 image, verify the application running on the local environment on port 8080, and view container logs.
1. Launch Docker container
Open Terminal in VS Code (Ctrl + ~) and run the container start command:
docker run -d --name productsservice-app -p 8080:8080 productsservice:1.0.0 Explanation of parameters:
-d: Run container in detached mode (background), without occupying the terminal window.
–name productsservice-app: Assigns an easily manageable name to the container.
-p 8080:8080: Maps port 8080 on the host machine to port 8080 inside the container.
productsservice:1.0.0: The image name created in lab 2.4.
2. Follow container logs
After running in the background, you have 2 ways to view the Spring Boot startup logs inside the container:
Option 1 (Using Terminal): docker logs -f productsservice-app (Press Ctrl + C to exit the log viewing screen without stopping the container).
Option 2 (Using the Docker Extension UI in VS Code):
Click the Docker icon in the vertical Activity Bar on the left. Expand the Containers section.
You will see the container productsservice-app with a green status (Running).
Right-click on that container -> select View Logs. VS Code will open a dedicated Terminal tab showing real-time logs.
When you see the familiar log line:
Started FcajSpringApplication in ... seconds => The Spring Boot application inside Docker has started successfully.
In case you encounter an error like in the image: This error occurs due to logging library conflicts.
Currently, both Logback (default Spring Boot logging) and Log4j2 exist simultaneously on the classpath. This happens because spring-boot-starter-logging was not completely excluded from all dependent starters (e.g., both spring-boot-starter-web and spring-boot-starter-actuator pull in starter-logging), or old Logback jar files remain in the target/dependency/BOOT-INF/lib folder.
To resolve this error, open pom.xml, check if you are using spring-boot-starter-actuator or any other starters besides spring-boot-starter-web. Add <exclusions> for all those starters.
Then perform the following steps in sequence to rebuild the image and verify the result: Remove the currently broken container: docker rm -f productsservice-app Clean the build directory, recompile, and extract the new JAR: .\mvnw.cmd clean package -DskipTests Remove-Item -Recurse -Force target\dependency -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue mkdir -Force target\dependency tar -xf (Get-Item target\*.jar).FullName -C target\dependency Rebuild the image (without cache): docker build --no-cache --platform linux/amd64 -t productsservice:1.0.0 . Run the container and check logs: docker run -d --name productsservice-app -p 8080:8080 productsservice:1.0.0 docker logs -f productsservice-app 3. Verify API (Verification) Open Postman or a Web Browser and test the endpoints:
Check Health endpoint (Actuator): URL: http://localhost:8080/actuator/health
Method: GET
Expected Result: Status 200 OK, JSON {“status”: “UP”}.
4. Stop local container to prevent port conflicts in subsequent steps
docker stop productsservice-app You have finished building and running the Docker image on your local machine. You are now ready to push the application to ECR.
If you encounter errors, you can clean the build directory following the steps starting from 1. Remove the currently broken container:

title: Create the VPC and private network
content:
Create the VPC and private network VpcStack creates a VPC across two Availability Zones. Each AZ receives a public subnet and a private subnet. Public subnets host resources needing direct Internet access, while private subnets host ECS tasks and internal load balancers.
The repository configures one NAT Gateway (natGateways: 1) because tasks in private subnets need to pull images from ECR, send logs to CloudWatch, and access AWS services. A NAT Gateway incurs hourly and data processing charges, so remember to destroy the stack after completing the workshop.

title: Push Docker image to ECR
content:
After the ECR repository fcaj-products-service has been successfully created, the final step in this section is to authenticate Docker CLI with the AWS ECR registry, tag the Spring Boot Docker image built previously, and push the image to AWS Cloud.
Note: You need to have Docker Desktop running to perform the following steps. If Docker Desktop is stopped, please start it.
1. Check Docker Image on Local Machine Open Terminal in VS Code and check the Docker image productsservice:1.0.0 (built successfully in step 2.4. Create Dockerfile and Build Docker Image):
docker images 2. Log in Docker to Amazon ECR Registry Docker CLI needs to be granted authentication permissions to communicate and push images to the private repository (Private registry) of your AWS account.
Run the following PowerShell commands to retrieve an authentication token via AWS CLI v2 and log in:
aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text aws ecr get-login-password --region ap-southeast-1 | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <account-id>.dkr.ecr.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com or
docker login Note: The authentication token returned from the aws ecr get-login-password command is valid for 12 hours. If you attempt to push an image after this period and encounter the error denied: Your authorization token has expired, simply re-run the login command above.
3. Tag Docker Image Following ECR Standards For Docker to know which repository on ECR to push the image to, the local image needs an additional tag in the format: <Registry-URI>/<Repository-Name>:<Tag>.
Run the tag command:
docker tag productsservice:1.0.0 <account-id>.dkr.ecr.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com/fcaj-products-service:1.0.0 Tag Management Rule:
The 1.0.0 tag represents the version of the application. When you upgrade or modify your Spring Boot source code in the future, increment the version number (for example: 1.0.1, 1.1.0) instead of using the latest tag or overwriting the old tag, allowing the ECS Fargate service to rollback when necessary.
4. Push Docker Image to Amazon ECR Run the docker push command to upload all layers of the image to the ECR repository:
docker push <account-id>.dkr.ecr.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com/fcaj-products-service:1.0.0 The terminal will show the upload progress for each layer:
5. Check Image on AWS ECR Console Return to your browser on the Amazon ECR service page > Repositories > click on the repository fcaj-products-service.
Click the Refresh icon on the toolbar.
You will see the image with tag 1.0.0 appear in the list along with detailed information: Image tag: 1.0.0 Artifact type: Container Image Pushed at: Upload timestamp Size: Compressed storage size Congratulations! You have completed creating an Amazon ECR repository using AWS CDK (TypeScript) and successfully pushed the Docker image of your Spring Boot application to AWS Cloud. This image is ready to be used in the next steps when building the ECS Fargate cluster.

title: Create DynamoDB products table
content:
Create DynamoDB products table In our microservices architecture powered by Amazon ECS Fargate, the database layer manages and persists product catalog data. This workshop leverages Amazon DynamoDB — a fully managed NoSQL key-value database service that delivers single-digit millisecond latency and seamless automatic scaling.
Under our Infrastructure as Code (IaC) modular design with AWS CDK, DynamoDbStack is defined and provisioned ahead of EcsStack to satisfy dependency requirements:
Initialize the products table: Configures the partition key as id (AttributeType.STRING). Grant IAM permissions: Exports the table construct (table: dynamodb.Table) so that EcsStack can grant read/write access (grantReadWriteData) to the ECS Fargate Task Role. Inject container environment variables: Provides the table name to populate the AWS_PRODUCTSDDB_NAME environment variable, enabling Spring Boot to connect seamlessly. By adopting the On-Demand (PAY_PER_REQUEST) billing mode, the DynamoDB table dynamically scales with request volume and incurs zero idle maintenance costs during lab workflows.

title: Run the application with ECS Fargate
content:
Run the application with ECS Fargate EcsStack creates the ECS cluster, Fargate task definition, Spring Boot container, X-Ray sidecar and ECS service. The task definition specifies 512 CPU units, 1024 MiB memory, port 8080, the CloudWatch log driver and ECR image tag 1.0.0.
The task role can read and write the DynamoDB table and write X-Ray traces. The execution role is used for startup operations such as pulling the image and sending logs.
The service runs one task in private subnets without a public IP. The deployment circuit breaker rolls back a failed deployment. The internal ALB listens on port 80 and forwards traffic to port 8080 on the task.
The health check calls GET /actuator/health. If a task is RUNNING but the target is unhealthy, inspect CloudWatch logs, port 8080, the health endpoint, security groups and subnet routes.
NlbStack creates an internal NLB in front of the ALB. The NLB uses AlbListenerTarget so the listener dependency is explicit. The NLB is the VPC Link entry point; it does not replace the ALB’s HTTP routing role.

title: Create API Gateway and VPC Link
content:
Create API Gateway and VPC Link In previous chapters, we built the entire backend infrastructure including the Amazon DynamoDB database, Amazon ECS Fargate container cluster, along with the Internal Application Load Balancer (ALB) and Internal Network Load Balancer (NLB) load balancing system. All of these resources are placed securely inside Private Subnets and have completely no public IP addresses.
To enable external client applications from the Internet (mobile apps, web frontends, Postman) to communicate securely with backend APIs, we will build Amazon API Gateway (HTTP API) combined with VPC Link.
Amazon API Gateway (HTTP API v2): Acts as the Public Entry Point, providing traffic management, CORS Preflight controls, and automatic scaling on demand with optimized cost (over 70% cheaper than traditional REST APIs).
VPC Link: Creates a “Private Tunnel” using Elastic Network Interfaces (ENI) placed in the Private Subnet of the VPC. VPC Link allows API Gateway to route requests directly to the internal Network Load Balancer without having to open public IPs for resources in the VPC.
HttpNlbIntegration: Standard integration from AWS CDK v2 that links the proxy route (/{proxy+}) with the listener of the NLB, forwarding all GET, POST, PUT, DELETE methods to the Spring Boot application.

title: Observability for AWS ECS with AWS X-Ray
content:
Observability for AWS ECS with AWS X-Ray The web container writes logs via AwsLogDriver with the products-service stream prefix. The xray-daemon container runs as a sidecar in the same task and receives traces via UDP port 2000. The application points to the sidecar using AWS_XRAY_DAEMON_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1:2000.
WebConfig creates segments for HTTP requests. DynamoDbConfig adds TracingInterceptor to the DynamoDB client to trace DynamoDB calls. The Task role is granted permissions to write X-Ray data.
To verify, call the API multiple times, open CloudWatch Logs in ECS, inspect the log streams of products-service and xray, then open the X-Ray Trace Map. If the sidecar is not running, check the image public.ecr.aws/xray/aws-xray-daemon, UDP port 2000, task role, and private network routing. X-Ray helps you see requests traveling through the application and DynamoDB. It does not replace logs; logs provide detailed events, while traces show which components requests pass through and how long each step takes.
Monitor X-Ray Traces Access CloudWatch and select Traces

title: Update image and deploy a new revision
content:
Update image and deploy a new revision When modifying Spring Boot code, build an image with a new tag. Do not reuse tag 1.0.0 because ECS may continue using the old task definition or learners may not know which version the task is running.
cd fcaj-spring .\mvnw.cmd clean package -DskipTests docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t fcaj-products-service:1.0.1 . docker tag fcaj-products-service:1.0.1 "$registry/fcaj-products-service:1.0.1" docker push "$registry/fcaj-products-service:1.0.1" Access AWS ECS -> Clusters -> fcaj-products-cluster -> Services -> fcaj-products-service -> select and click FORCE NEW DEPLOYMENT:
Open cdk/lib/ecs-stack.ts and change the image tag from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1. Then build TypeScript and deploy the ECS stack:
cd ..\cdk npm run build npx cdk deploy --all --require-approval never CDK creates a new task definition revision. ECS rolling deployment will launch the new task, wait for health check, and stop the old task according to deployment configuration.
Images to add later: /images/UPDATE/12-update.

title: Clean up resources
content:
Clean up resources The lab creates a NAT Gateway, VPC Link, load balancers, ECS task, ECR repository, DynamoDB table, CloudWatch log group, and IAM roles. Some of these resources will continue to incur costs if left running.
Delete all stacks using the command:
cd cdk npx cdk destroy --all --force Before deleting, check whether DynamoDB contains any data that needs to be kept. After the command completes, open CloudFormation, ECS, ECR, DynamoDB, VPC, and API Gateway to confirm that resources have been deleted. The ECR repository and DynamoDB table are configured with DESTROY removal policies for lab purposes.
Tip for handling stuck ECR DELETE_FAILED errors: If the ECR Repository reports an error that it cannot be deleted because it still contains images, run the force delete command from the AWS CLI:
Access Cloudformation Console -> select the stuck stack. Or use AWS CLI to remove the stuck stack: aws ecr delete-repository --repository-name fcaj-products-service --region ap-southeast-1 --force
